title: Resisting the Cat-Torturer in the Casa de Nariño
author: Hamza Shehryar
content:
August 7 will be a dark day, for it is when Colombia's presidential turnover
is set to take place. On this day, which marks the anniversary of the Battle
of Boyacá – the decisive 1819 battle in which Simón Bolívar's army defeated
Spanish troops to secure Colombia's independence – outgoing president Gustavo
Petro will hand over power to Abelardo de la Espriella, Colombia's new
president-elect.

However, it is dubious whether "elect" is an adequate word to describe the
far-right de la Espriella or his triumph in the election runoff on June 21. It
was a process that, if not outright compromised, certainly embodied
irregularities that, had they crowned an anti-imperialist or Bolivarian
candidate, would have faced swift criticism, condemnation and sanctions from
the US, its Western allies, and their election observers. Fortunately for
these imperial institutions, which mask their ugly faces under the façade of
liberalism, Colombia’s new president will not need any of that; rather, he
will serve US interests as a de facto viceroy – especially as he himself is a
US citizen.

It is no secret that de la Espriella – who proudly flaunts the fact that he
voted for Trump in the 2024 US presidential election – lived in Miami for a
decade and only returned to the country of his birth to campaign. During his
time in Miami, de la Espriella, a lawyer, represented political figures allied
with paramilitaries, such as former congresswoman Eleonora Pineda and former
senator Dieb Maloof. From 2013 to 2019, he also served as legal counsel to
Alex Saab, who was later indicted in the United States on charges including
money laundering and operating as a financial agent for the Venezuelan
government of Nicolás Maduro. You couldn't make it up.

In fact, during the final days of his election campaign, de la Espriella's
wife, Ana Lucía Pineda,
[remarked](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DY5gHNqDpLM/) that if her husband
lost the election, they would simply return to their comfortable life in
Miami. Throughout this campaign, de la Espriella positioned himself in the
mould of Javier Milei in Argentina, and Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil: an
obedient vassal to the imperial whims of Donald Trump and US hegemony – a
Delcy Rodriguez, only without a gun to his head.

He openly leveraged Donald Trump's blatant disregard for international law and
the imperial fervour of the "Donroe Doctrine" in Latin America to scare
Colombians away from voting for Iván Cepeda, the anti-imperialist candidate of
Petro's Historic Pact coalition. His campaign was explicitly endorsed by
Donald Trump – unquestionably a form of external political pressure, even if
conveniently disregarded by the very people who rail against foreign
intervention in elections closer to home. But that is merely the tip of an
iceberg built not just by the US, but by Israel as well.

Petro [explicitly accused](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/colombias-petro-
accuses-israeli-cyberfirm-blackcore-of-election-interference/3994677)
BlackCore, an Israeli cyber-intelligence firm, of conducting a "massive
digital disinformation campaign" to manipulate the electorate. He alleged that
the firm deployed approximately 500,000 automated "bot" accounts to
disseminate "millions of lies" about himself and Cepeda across social media
platforms to sway public perception.

Colombian and American reactionaries and private media outlets have framed
these accusations as the ravings of a bitter outgoing president. However,
these allegations cannot be readily dismissed, coming as they do in the
immediate aftermath of [Hondurasgate](https://hondurasgate.ch) – an exposé by
journalists with _Canal Red_ detailing a [transnational disinformation
network](https://latinoamerica21.com/en/hondurasgate-and-the-tragedy-of-
automatic-alignment-in-latin-america/) involving actors from Honduras,
Argentina, Israel, and the United States colluding to influence regional
politics and destabilise progressive governments across Latin America,
including those of Petro and Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum.

Additionally, electoral pressures came directly from Colombian corporations
and the ruling class heading them, too. Independent Colombian media outlet
_Revista Raya_ [reported on an internal Ministry of Labour
document](https://revistaraya.com/mas-de-50-empresas-privadas-fueron-
denunciadas-por-presionar-a-sus-empleados-para-votar-por-de-la-espriella.html)
detailing complaints from employees across 59 companies, in which workers
alleged that employers threatened them with job loss or claimed their
companies would be "expropriated" if Cepeda won, effectively coercing them to
vote for de la Espriella. Those from Global South countries hollowed out by
imperialism and enforced neoliberal austerity will recognise how frequently
the landowning and corporate class acts to coerce workers into supporting
elite-backed candidates.

Despite these covert and overt interventions, de la Espriella barely prevailed
in the runoff. He scraped through with 49.66% of the vote against Cepeda's
48.70%, the narrowest margin of victory ever recorded in a Colombian
presidential election. Immediately, this machismo figure, cut from the same
cloth as Donald Trump and Javier Milei, and who [infamously boasted
of](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L_jh-gnvT6g&t=4s) tying firecrackers to
cats and watching them explode as a child, announced he would restore
Colombia's ties with the apartheid state of Israel (which Petro severed,
alongside coal exports) and move Colombia's embassy to Jerusalem. This
decision is telling, for it only lends further credence to Petro's claims of
Israeli meddling in the electoral process.

Similarly, de la Espriella has vowed to suspend Colombia's Palestinian
embassy, cut ties with Cuba and Nicaragua (but maintain a “constructive”
relationship with Delcy Rodriguez’s – [Marco
Rubio’s](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/11/us/politics/how-marco-rubio-runs-
venezuela.html) – Venezuela), join Trump’s murderous Shield of the Americas
alliance and enforce the laissez-faire economic policies that have ravaged
working people across Latin America for the profits of US companies for
decades. Ultimately, the Colombian-American will be less Colombian, more
American in who his agenda will serve.

So, August 7, the day the cat torturer enters the Casa de Nariño, the office
of the executive branch in Bogotá, will be a dark day for all of us – and
certainly for the millions of Colombians who rejected de la Espriella’s odious
politics and whose lives were directly improved by Petro's progressive
economic agenda, which was defined by structural reform through aggressive
state intervention.

Petro achieved a landmark 23.7% combined rise in minimum wage by 2026,
alongside comprehensive labour reforms mandating indefinite contracts as
standard and expanding evening and holiday pay surcharges for the working
class. At the same time, his government expanded social spending to deliver
direct monthly transfers to female-headed households in extreme poverty, as
well as universal tuition-free public higher education for low-income
students. These policies delivered measurable reductions in both national
poverty and unemployment. According to official statistics, monetary poverty
dropped from 36.6% in 2022 to 31.8% in 2024, lifting over 1.3 million
Colombians out of poverty, while unemployment fell from 11.2% in 2022 to 8.29%
by 2025, reaching the lowest annual rate recorded in over two decades.

And this is without mentioning Petro’s progressive climate record, which
included banning non-conventional fossil fuel extraction, such as fracking,
and making Colombia the first major fossil-fuel-producing nation to endorse
the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty at COP28. Most, if not all, of this
will be undone by the incoming government, the cabinet of which is set to be
[riddled with corrupt, establishment
figures](https://www.thebogotapost.com/meet-the-incoming-cabinet-appointed-by-
colombias-next-president/56632/) from erstwhile Colombian administrations.

As he concludes his historic term as Colombia's first left-wing leader, with
an approval rating floating around 50% – among the highest for an outgoing
Colombian president in modern history – Petro described the election process
and de la Espriella's ascendancy starkly: "The hardest blow to national
sovereignty since the Spanish reconquest."

It harkens back to the infamous words uttered by another anti-imperialist
Latin American leader in 2008, when, following a cross-border raid by the
Colombian military into Ecuador that killed a FARC commander, Hugo Chávez
called Colombia the ["Israel of Latin
America"](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/southamerica/venezuela/5901163/Hugo-
Chavez-Colombia-is-Israel-of-Latin-America.html), arguing that just as
Washington used Israel as its proxy in the Middle East, it sought to transform
Colombia into an enforcement arm in Latin America to block regional unity.
This claim was embraced by then Colombian president Álvaro Uribe. Petro
inverted this dynamic, transforming the country from a steadfast vassal of
empire to a state [standing alongside the wretched of the
earth](https://thehaguegroup.org/home/). Now, the old status quo is returning.

It may feel like a grim moment for anti-imperialists in Latin America and
beyond, but the fight is far from over. Protests broke out shortly after
election results were announced in Bogotá and Cali, and Petro has called on
everyone who values sovereignty and solidarity to take to the streets in
sustained protest against the incoming government. Meanwhile, the Historic
Pact retains a powerful presence in both chambers of the Colombian Congress
following gains in the March legislative elections. It will exert resistance
as de la Espriella inevitably attempts to gut the state to enrich his allies
and benefactors.

The gains made under Petro's outgoing government cannot be easily dismantled
if there is unrelenting popular pressure against the "outsider" who, like
Trump, is anti-establishment in branding only. Like [those
rejecting](https://jacobin.com/2026/05/bolivia-indigenous-land-rights-
privatization-paz) the authoritarian neoliberal policies of Rodrigo Paz in
Bolivia, [those fighting](https://www.dropsitenews.com/p/state-killings-in-
pakistan-as-kashmir) the military establishment in Pakistan, [those
documenting and
resisting](https://www.thenation.com/article/activism/occupied-minnesota-west-
bank/) the tyranny of ICE in the United States, and [those “cockroaches”
standing up](https://progressive.international/wire/2026-07-24-cockroach-
democracy-unarmed-and-dangerous/en/) to fascism, corruption and crony
capitalism in India, Colombians, too, will resist – and socialists and
internationalists around the world must stand firmly in their support.

We must remain unified against the blight of imperialism and neoliberalism to
build a collective future rooted in dignity – a future in which our collective
existence amounts to more than one where the many endlessly tighten their
belts to generate unimaginable wealth for the few who exploit them; the
insulated few who descend to any low to add another dollar to their stock
portfolios and offshore bank accounts.

The post [Resisting the Cat-Torturer in the Casa de
Nariño](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/08/06/resisting-the-cat-torturer-in-
the-casa-de-narino/) appeared first on
[CounterPunch.org](https://www.counterpunch.org).
